question: Can model-Hessian directions reduce expensive query-only gate calibration, and what fails as the model-device gap grows?

method.name: Model-informed derivative-free closed-loop calibration
method.tool: JAX model derivatives, finite-shot black-box device, coordinate scans, and SciPy COBYQA
method.note: An open-loop model optimum supplies the leading Hessian directions. The device returns only a finite-shot scalar gate loss. Closed-loop optimization is restricted to a model-defined affine subspace; a failed device-only certificate may trigger a model-side basis update at the current pulse.

settings.certificate: 7 repeated queries; Wilson upper bound with z=1.96 (conservative relative to a nominal one-sided 95% bound)

information_boundary: The online optimizer receives only scalar finite-shot losses. Held-out Hamiltonians, mismatch strength, endpoint Jacobians, gradients, and exact fidelities are hidden and used only for offline scoring.

mismatch.normalization: Frobenius norm of DeltaH equals the Frobenius norm of H0

figures.plots: Intrinsic Hessian rank and single-qubit closed-loop query efficiency

results.why: Observed ranks equal d^2-1 for d=2 and d=4; for the single-qubit device at epsilon=0.3, the informed k=3 space certifies all runs with a 25-query median, while random k=3 certifies none and the raw 20-dimensional space needs a 126-query median.

figures.plots: Fixed-space failure under drift mismatch and device-triggered adaptive recovery

results.why: At epsilon=0.5, fixed nominal k=15 certifies only 20% of runs; increasing the fixed dimension improves success but costs more queries. Triggered k=15-to-20 relinearization certifies all 45 held-out runs across epsilon=0.1, 0.3, and 0.5.
